1.text: We'll call to pick a scenario for the occasion and group size and decide where to play: at your place or a club partner's venue.

5.title: The game
5.text: The host arrives early and sets everything up — all you do is play.

corporate.price: It depends on the format, venue, length and number of guests. Write to us and we'll send a quote for your event.

0.q: How many people do we need?
0.a: You can play from 6 people. For larger groups we run several tables at once.

1.a: Usually 2–3 hours, enough for several games. One game lasts 30–60 minutes.

2.q: Does anyone need to know the rules?
2.a: No. The host explains the rules at the start and runs the first game as practice.

3.q: Which language do we play in?
3.a: English, Czech, Russian or Ukrainian. Each host's languages are shown on their card in the Hosts section above.

4.q: Can you come to us or to another city?
4.a: Yes. We come to your office, a café, a restaurant or another venue and bring the props — or suggest one of our partner venues. We run games beyond the Czech Republic, in other cities and countries too: just mention it in your request.

5.q: How far ahead should we book?
5.a: Ideally 2–4 weeks ahead, and even earlier for December: pre-Christmas dates go fast.

history.title: Club history
history.lead: MafiaCL has been playing since 2011. The club has moved through three cities, but the essentials stayed the same: fair competitive mafia, strong hosts and people you want to come back to.

steps.title: The beginning: MafiaCL Kremenchug
steps.text: MafiaCL is born in Kremenchuk, Ukraine — the first club under this name, founded by YeS (Ievgen Sokolskyi).

steps.title: Student club Mafia HNEU
steps.text: The same year the student club Mafia HNEU plays at Kharkiv National University of Economics — the start of the club's Kharkiv chapter.

steps.title: Moving to Kharkiv
steps.text: The club carries on in Kharkiv, adding rated seasons, mini-tournaments, a club code, a student league and open lessons of a mafia school.

steps.title: Season IV — the longest one
steps.text: 205 rated games and 33 mini-tournaments. The mafia won 110 games, the town 95. Season champion: Persik, runner-up Sarkasm, third Din. The same year YeS earns the FIIM grandmaster title.

steps.title: Season V and the world championship
steps.text: A season that lasts the whole year. Club players represent Kharkiv with two teams at the Team World Mafia Championship in Kyiv. The Slobozhanshchyna Cup draws 60 participants from 16 cities.

steps.title: Season VI and the launch of Mafia Champions League
steps.text: A record season with 370 rated games; champion: Din. The first season of Mafia Champions League starts — a league of qualifying series and a final. The Slobozhanshchyna Cup brings together 60 players from 13 cities, and Mafia Stars and the Maf-Marathon, a 24-hour pairs tournament, are held for the first time.

steps.title: An 80-player Slobozhanshchyna Cup
steps.text: The club's main summer tournament draws 80 participants; Sarkasm wins. The first Mafia Champions League final: 105 games in the season, champion Din. The first Ukrainian Students Tournament is held, and Flash becomes Season VII champion.

steps.title: 80 players for the second year running
steps.text: The Slobozhanshchyna Cup again draws 80 participants; the winner is 22. Mafia Stars goes national as Mafia Stars Ukraine, won by Flash. Benjamin wins MCL 2017/2018 and Snow wins Season VIII.

steps.title: The league grows
steps.text: Mafia Champions League 2018/2019: 106 games in the season and a 8,000 UAH prize fund; Shershen wins. Flash wins Mafia Stars Ukraine for the second year in a row.

steps.title: Mafia Champions League 2019/2020
steps.text: 116 games in the season and a 10,000 UAH prize fund; champion: Kira. Marta wins the Slobozhanshchyna Cup.

steps.title: Mafia Stars Europe
steps.text: The fifth and final season of the club's tournament series: qualifying series in several cities, semi-finals and a 20-player final on 9–10 October 2021. A 4★ Mafia World Tour event with about 180 participants. The same year Mafia Champions League 2020/2021 has 136 games and a 12,000 UAH prize fund, won by Shershen. From 2022 the league runs two parallel finals — in Ukraine and in Europe.

steps.title: MafiaCL in Prague
steps.text: The club starts playing in Prague and builds a new community — players from Czechia, Ukraine and all over Europe.

steps.title: Today
steps.text: Tuesdays: Premier League mini-tournaments at AURA. Sundays: MafiaCL Arena at POP PAUSE. In November Prague hosts the MCL Europe 2026 final, and in January 2027 MafiaCL Kings, the club's main tournament.

code.title: Club code
code.lead: A short set of rules on how we play and how we behave at the club. The code applies at every MafiaCL game and tournament.

values.name: Respect
values.text: For players, the host and the venue. We argue with reasons, never with insults.

values.name: Trust
values.text: Fair play with no deals, bets or oaths. We accept the host's decisions at the table.

values.name: Focus
values.text: While the game is on, we're in it: no phones, side talk or stray objects on the table.

values.name: Responsibility
values.text: For your sign-up, your time and your words — at the table and after the game.

parts.title: At the table
items: We play by classic mafia rules and the tournament regulations; rule nuances are announced before the games start.
We address each other formally and end every speech with “Thank you”.
Bets, oaths and appeals to outside circumstances are forbidden — the team loses the game for them.
No gestures or sounds at night: touching above the table means removal, below the table a foul.
Left the table? Poker face on: any word or gesture after leaving can count as a hint.
Only game items on the table: phones, earphones, coins and the like go away.

parts.title: House rules
parts.intro: A little serious and a little tongue-in-cheek — taken from our old club posters.
items: Signed up? Be on time: lateness is penalised under the regulations, and we don't wait for the 10th player.
Can't make it? Cancel in advance so another player gets the seat.
Seagulls shout on the beach, mafia players don't. Silence at every table during a game.
No swearing. Insulting a player means a ban.
We're guests of our partners: respect the venue, its staff and other guests.
Staying for the post-game review — great. Disputes are discussed after the game, not during it.

parts.title: The host and disputes
items: The host's decision at the table is final. It can be explained after the game.
If you disagree, talk to the organiser after the game: we'll review the situation under the regulations.
The host may give a warning, a foul or remove a player from the table.

parts.title: Breaking the code
items: For serious or repeated violations, the club management may bar a player from club games.
The list of current bans is published under Bans.

learn.lead: Never played before? That's fine — most of our players once came for the first time too. Here's everything worth knowing before your first game.

0.title: Pick a game
0.text: The schedule is on the Play page. The easiest start is a Tuesday mini-tournament or the Sunday MafiaCL Arena.

1.title: Sign up
1.text: Sign up on the site or message us on Telegram. You don't need to know the rules.

2.title: Come a bit early
2.text: 10–15 minutes before the start: meet the host and players and take your seat.

3.title: Play
3.text: The host explains the rules and helps along the way. The first games are for getting the hang of it — mistakes are fine.

learn.what: A team game of logic, attention and persuasion. Ten players sit at the table with a host who acts as judge. Roles are dealt secretly, everyone has a number and equal time to speak, and decisions are made by vote. You don't need to act: listening, noticing details and arguing your case matter more. A game lasts about an hour and results count towards the club rating.
learn.rolesLead: Each game has 7 civilians and 3 mafia. Only you know your role.

civilian.title: Civilian
civilian.text: Doesn't know who the mafia are. Their weapons are logic, attention and the vote.

sheriff.title: Sheriff
sheriff.text: Checks one player every night and learns whether they are mafia.

mafia.title: Mafia
mafia.text: Knows their partners. At night they choose together whom to eliminate; by day they pose as civilians.

don.title: Don
don.text: Head of the mafia: shoots with the team and hunts for the Sheriff every night.

0.title: Roles are dealt
0.text: Everyone secretly draws a role card and puts on a mask when the host calls night.

1.title: First night
1.text: The mafia open their eyes and silently agree on their plan. The Sheriff and the Don show themselves to the host.

2.title: Day
2.text: Each player in turn has a minute to speak and can nominate someone they suspect.

3.title: Vote
3.text: The player with the most votes leaves the table and gets a farewell minute.

4.title: Night
4.text: The mafia shoot, the Don looks for the Sheriff, the Sheriff checks. In the morning the host announces who is out. Civilians win when no mafia are left; the mafia win when they equal the civilians in number.

etiquette.0: Speak only during your time — don't interrupt others.
etiquette.1: Mask on at night: no peeking and no gestures.
etiquette.3: No oaths, bets or appeals to anything outside the game.
etiquette.4: Respect your opponents and the host's decisions.
etiquette.5: The host gives fouls for violations; on the fourth foul a player leaves the table.

learn.codeNote: More about the club's values and ethics —
learn.more: Our YouTube channel has recorded games and tournaments with commentary, and Telegram has announcements, results and club news. But the best way to learn is to come and play.

faq.lead: Answers to the questions people ask most before their first game.

rules.q: Do I need to know the rules?
rules.a: No. The host explains them before the game and helps along the way. A short version is on the For new players page.

alone.a: Yes, most people do. You get to know each other quickly at the table — that's what the game is for.

players.q: How many people play at a table?
players.a: Ten players and a host. If more sign up, we open a second table.

duration.a: One game takes about an hour. A club evening is several games in a row, so plan on 3–4 hours.

age.a: Club games are for adults. For children and teenagers we have a separate format — kids' mafia.

when.q: When and where do you play?
when.a: Tuesdays at 18:45 — mini-tournaments at Aura Shisha & Karaoke; Sundays at 14:00 — MafiaCL Arena at POP PAUSE Popcorn Café. The current schedule is on the Play page.

signup.a: On the Play page or via our Telegram bot. Tuesdays use pre-registration: membership holders get priority, everyone else is confirmed in order.

price.a: The price is listed in each game's announcement. Regular players can get a membership: it gives priority when signing up and covers the evening fee.

season.q: What are the season and rating?
season.a: Every game earns points towards the season rating. The season's best players reach the final and compete for the club championship.

language.q: What language do you play in?
language.a: Club games are usually in Russian and Ukrainian. Corporate events are also run in English and Czech.

corporate.q: Can we book a game for our company?
corporate.a: Yes: corporate events, birthdays, parties with friends — at your place or a partner venue. Details and requests are on the Corporate page.

kids.q: Do you have games for children?
kids.a: Yes, kids' mafia — with adapted rules and a host, birthdays included.

contact.a: Message the club's founder on Telegram @Yes1911 — we'll reply.

faq.still: Didn't find your answer? Message us — or just come to a game.

rules.title: Mafgame game rules
rules.lead: A short summary of the Mafgame federation's sport mafia rules in our own words, split into sections so it reads well on a phone. Federation tournaments — including those the club hosts — are played under these rules. Club rating points follow each season's regulations.
rules.sourceNote: The official full text, including referee gestures and the complete list of penalties, is on the Mafgame federation website. Where they differ, the official text applies.

sections.title: Basics
items: Ten players at the table. Cards are dealt at random: 7 red (civilians, including the Sheriff) and 3 black (mafia, including the Don).
The game is run by the referee (host), who announces the start, every phase and the end. Side referees may assist.
Day (discussion and voting) and night (shooting, the Don's check, the Sheriff's check) alternate until the game ends.
Red wins when no black players are left. Black wins when there are as many black players as red, or more. The referee immediately announces “Stop game, red wins” or “…black wins”.

sections.title: Table, equipment and language
items: A table for 10, with a number plate and a mask at every seat. Music is needed for the night.

Finals and tournaments of 5 stars and above are played in Russian or English (except tournaments in Ukraine). Qualifying stages can be in any language that suits all players and referees, provided everyone is ready to switch to Russian or English in the final. Exceptions are agreed with the referee committee.

sections.title: Players
items: Before the game, players hand the referee their watches, sunglasses, phones and other items.

Equipment must not get in the way, offend anyone or give an advantage. Your own mask only with the table referee's permission. Special devices or a different night posture must be agreed with the head referee in advance.

sections.title: Dealing and the first night
items: Seats are drawn at random or taken from the tournament seating. At “night falls” everyone puts on their mask.
Hearing their number, a player shows it on their fingers, takes off the mask, looks at the card the referee counted out from the deck on the table, and puts the mask back on.
The deal night: black players take off their masks and meet — the only night they see each other. The Don shows himself with a gesture and sets the shooting order. All of this takes exactly 1 minute.
Then, on the referee's call, the Don and the Sheriff raise a hand without taking off their masks. After that — 30 seconds of free posture.

sections.title: Day
items: At “morning” the masks come off. Every player gets 1 minute to speak. Player 1 opens the first day; each next day is opened by the player after the one who opened the previous round.
Address players by nickname or number, and the referee as “Mr/Ms Referee” or “Host”. A speech ends with “pass” or “thank you”.

You can nominate one player per day, in the present tense: “I nominate number…”. The referee answers “accepted”. If several numbers are named, the first one not yet nominated is accepted. Nominations cannot be withdrawn.
After their farewell minute, a player leaves the table straight away. Gestures from those still at the table before the referee resumes the game are a foul.

sections.title: Voting
items: Only nominated players are voted on, in the order they were nominated. The referee repeats the list twice before the vote.

A vote is a fist with the thumb up on the table, for about 1.5 seconds until “stop” or “thank you”; late votes do not count. Keep your hand on the table until the referee announces the count. You can vote for one candidate only; anyone who doesn't vote has their vote go to the last nominee.
On the first day there is no vote if only one player is nominated. From the second day on, a sole nominee leaves automatically.
The player with the most votes leaves the game. Their role is not revealed; they get a 1-minute farewell speech.
On a tie, the tied players get 30 seconds each, then a revote. If the same players tie again, the referee asks “all of them leave the table?”: they leave only if more than half vote for it.
With 9 players at the table, three cannot be voted out together (except after the third night if the Sheriff has made at least two checks). On the first day, half the table cannot be voted out.
The referee decides the vote count. In a dispute, they must call a technical pause straight away and review the stream; the decision after the review is final.

sections.title: Night
items: The referee counts numbers 1 to 10 and the black players “shoot” with eyes closed using a hand gesture. If all of them shoot the same player, that player is out in the morning and gets a farewell minute. Any mismatch or missing shot is a miss.

The Don (10 seconds) looks for the Sheriff: the referee repeats the number and shows “sheriff” or “not sheriff”. The Sheriff (10 seconds) checks a player: thumb up — red, thumb down — black. Each has one check per night.

Night posture: straight back, arms crossed on the shoulders, head tilted forward. At night you may not talk, whisper, touch others, eat or drink. The mask on an elastic band must cover the eyes tightly and must not be held with the hands; hats and glasses come off.

sections.title: Best move
items: The player killed on the first night after the deal names three numbers they believe are black, with 20 seconds to think. Then it's morning and their farewell minute.
Any extra information or addressing other players ends the best move: only the numbers already named count. Numbers cannot be changed, except for an obvious slip of the tongue.
If two or more players left the table on the first day, the player killed on the first night has no best move.

sections.title: Fouls and penalties
items: 3 fouls — the player skips their next speech but can still nominate. A 4th or disqualifying foul — removal with no last word.

Foul: loud knocking, arguing with the referee and unethical behaviour, touching and excessive gestures during the day, talking outside your minute, pulling your hand away or campaigning during a vote, shouting.

Removal: insults (including veiled or joking ones about health, race, gender, orientation, religion, nationality, or mentions of suicide), breaking night rules, leaving the table without permission, crying, an incorrect voting gesture, swearing, peeking, speaking a language the table doesn't understand, non-game attempts to prove a role, citing the best move as proof, hidden whispering.

The other team wins: oaths, pleading, blackmail, threats, bribery and bets; appeals to religion or ethics (“God knows I'm red”); a Sheriff proving the role with night information; hints from the audience.
Removal from the tournament: deliberate peeking, insulting the referee, threats of violence.

sections.title: Special situations
items: After a removal for a 4th or disqualifying foul, the next vote does not take place (unless the removed player was leaving anyway — killed at night or voted out). If two or more players are removed in one phase, one vote is skipped.
Three nights in a row with nobody leaving — a draw. There is never a vote to remove everyone at the table. If a player leaves by the deciding vote or shot and the game ends, they get no last word.
Night removals are announced so as not to reveal roles. From the moment of the violation the player counts as a spectator: if they pass on information, their team loses.

sections.title: Tournament points
items: A win gives 0.75 points to every player of the team; a loss or a draw gives 0.
Best move by a red player or the Sheriff: three black — +0.4, two — +0.25.

Referee extra points — no more than 2.0 per game in total. A player gets +0.1 to +0.8 (+0.8 only with the referee committee's approval); a player on the losing team gets up to +0.5. No extra points on a draw. Best-move points count towards the same assessment.

Referee penalties of −0.2 or −0.4 for mistakes that hurt your own team (full list in the federation rules). Removal from the table — −0.5; costing your team the game — −0.75. Being late for a round — from −0.2 up to being replaced.
A red player or Sheriff killed on the first night gets compensation of up to 0.4 points when red loses; it grows with the number of such first-night kills over the tournament.
On equal points, the higher place goes to more extra points, then fewer penalties, more first-night deaths, more wins as Sheriff, then as Don, and finally earlier registration.

sections.title: Protests and replays
items: A protest is written in the game record within 15 minutes of the end of the game. The head referee or the appeal committee reviews it, video included; the decision is final within the tournament.
If a non-game advantage or non-game proof of a role decided the game, the result may be changed and the player at fault gets −0.75.
A replay is ordered after an irreparable technical error by the referee or force majeure: seating changes, disciplinary penalties stay.
Appeals about extra points — only in writing to the table referee and within the set deadlines.

sections.title: Basics
items: Ten players sit at the table. Cards are dealt at random: 7 red (town, including the Sheriff) and 3 black (mafia, including the Don).
The game is run by a certified referee, who may be helped by side referees. Day and night alternate until one team wins.
Red wins when no black players are left. Black wins when there are as many black players as red, or more.
A player is out when voted out during the day, shot at night, or given a disqualifying foul.
If after a vote black needs only one more successful shot to win, black wins straight away, with no night shooting.

sections.title: Players, table and language
items: Gear must not be dangerous, offensive or give an advantage. If the referee asks, phones are handed in before the game (silenced or switched off). Your own mask only after the referee has checked and approved it.
Hats, glasses and anything reflective come off before night.
Each seat has a number and a mask on an elastic band that fully covers the eyes. Night needs music.
Official languages of the game: Ukrainian, English and Russian.

sections.title: Dealing and the first night
items: The referee draws seats before the game, or they come from the tournament schedule. At "night falls" everyone puts on their mask.

Players take a card in turn with their eyes closed, look at the role and put the mask back on. Once the 10th player has a role, everyone takes the night position: arms crossed on the shoulders, head tilted forward about 45°.
The meeting: black players take off their masks and see each other — the only night they do. The Don identifies himself with a gesture and sets the shooting order. All of this takes exactly 1 minute.
Then 1 minute of relaxed position: the head stays tilted, but light hand movement and swaying to the music are allowed. After that morning comes.

sections.title: Day
items: Masks are off during the day and may not be put on. Each player has 1 minute. Player 1 opens day zero; each later day is opened by the player after the one who opened the previous round.
Players are addressed by nickname or number, the referee as "Mr/Madam Referee" or "Host". A speech ends with "pass" or "thank you".
Each day you may nominate one player, in the present tense: "I nominate player No. …". The referee confirms: "accepted".

sections.title: Voting
items: Before the vote the referee reads the nominees twice. Voting follows the order of nomination; from this moment gestures and campaigning are penalised, up to disqualification.

A vote is a fist placed upright on the table right after the number is called, before "stop" or "thank you" (about 1.5 seconds). Keep the hand on the table until the referee announces the count; a hand pulled back still counts.
You may vote for only one nominee. A player who does not vote gives the vote to the last nominee.
On day zero there is no vote if only one player is nominated. On later days a sole nominee receives all the votes.

On a tie, the tied players get 30 seconds each and there is a revote. If the votes split evenly between the same players again, the referee asks who wants all of them to leave: they go only if a majority votes for it.
With 9 players, three cannot be voted out together on the first day only — night falls straight away instead. The whole table can never be voted out.
The role of a player who leaves is not revealed; they get a 1-minute last word.

sections.title: Night
items: From the second night the mafia shoots: the referee counts from 1 to 10 and black players "pull the trigger" with a raised hand. If all black players shoot the same player, that player is killed; anything else is a miss.
Then the Don wakes up to look for the Sheriff, and after him the Sheriff checks any player. Each check takes no more than 10 seconds, one check per night.
At night you may not talk, sing, dance, touch others, eat, drink or smoke. You may not hold the mask with your hands.

sections.title: Key five
items: A red player killed on the first night may, within 30 seconds, name one to five numbers and their colours. Correct colours earn points, mistakes cost points.
A player who names no colour at all gets −0.1.
Named numbers cannot be changed or added to. If the player starts saying anything other than numbers, addresses the table or provokes a reaction, the key five is over.
There is no key five if two or more players were voted out on day zero.

sections.title: Fouls and penalties
items: A foul is given for things like speaking outside your minute (even a whisper or clear mouthing), excessive gestures, touching others during the day, knocking on the table, arguing with the referee, voting incorrectly, or gestures outside your own space.
Three fouls: the player stays silent in their next minute but may still nominate. A fourth foul: the player leaves at once with no last word.

A disqualifying foul means leaving the table at once: leaving without permission, touching at night, talking at night, insults, swearing, peeking, appealing to one's word of honour, God or other non-game values, requests about the key five, hidden whispering into someone's ear, switching to a foreign language to hide information, crying, or excessive emotion to prove a role.
The team loses the game for oaths and bets, blackmail, threats and bribery, hints from the audience, and for a Sheriff proving the role with night information.
Peeking or insulting the referee gets a player removed from the tournament.

sections.title: Special situations
items: If a player leaves with a fourth or disqualifying foul, the next vote is skipped (unless that player was being voted out or had been killed).
If nobody leaves the table for three nights in a row, the game is a draw after the third night.
A player with three fouls may speak in a tie-break, and gets 30 seconds in a guessing round of 3–4 players.
Once a vote or a kill decides the game, the referee announces the win at once; there is no last word.
The head referee together with the RD may order a replay: a wrong check shown, a shot counted wrongly, a mistaken disqualification, outside information leaking in, or force majeure.

sections.title: Tournament points
items: A win gives 1 point to every player of the winning team. A loss or a draw gives 0.
Disqualification from the table: −0.5 to the final rating; a team-loss penalty (PPK): −0.7.
Best move: three black players correctly named in the key five give +0.6, two give +0.4.

The referee may give extra points to up to seven players, 3.4 in total at most (3.6 with the head referee's approval). Winners get 0.2 to 1 (1.3 only with the head referee's approval), losers 0.2 to 0.8.
Referee points and best-move points do not add up — the larger one counts. Players at the table when a draw is declared get no extra points.

Destructive mistakes cost −0.3 or −0.5: for example voting out your own player in the critical round, a miss despite a clear call, a Sheriff making no checks, a Don who sets no shooting order. The full list is in the official text.

sections.title: Ci compensation
items: A red player killed on the first night whose team then loses gets Ci compensation — their average extra points in full games of the same event.
With three full games or fewer, the extra points are divided by 3; after that, by the actual number of games.
Compensation raises the game result to the Ci level if the extra points and penalties for that game came out lower. If they are higher, the actual result counts.

sections.title: Standings and awards
items: The final place is by the total of base and extra points. Ties are broken by extra points, then number of wins, fewer penalties, higher share of first-night kills, and finally by lot. Team standings work the same way.
MVP: the most extra points. Best red and Best black: total extra points in those roles. Most dangerous player: the most first-night kills.
A protest about a result must be filed in writing within 60 minutes after the referee enters the game. The head referee or the RD member on duty reviews it, video included; the decision is final.

sections.title: Glossary
items: Day zero — the first day after the mafia meeting. Day one — the one after it.
Critical round — when voting out a red player would give the mafia the win (usually with 7–8 players). Guessing round — with three or four players left.
Dynamic call — a shot target agreed during the day discussion.
Tie-break ("car crash") — equal votes. Splitting — deliberately sharing votes equally. Lift — all players who tied twice leave together.
Balance — voting out in turn two players who are certainly on different teams. Counterweight — voting out two players who call each other black.
RD — the Emotion Games referee department.
